text: At seven oclock the coffee was made. <break time="0.8s" /> And the frying pan was ready. <break time="0.8s" /> On the back of the stove. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim was never late. <break time="0.8s" /> Della held the chain in her hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat on the corner of the table. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the door. <break time="0.8s" /> She heard his step on the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> And for a moment. <break time="0.8s" /> She turned white. <break time="0.8s" /> Please God. <break time="0.8s" /> Make him think. <break time="0.8s" /> I am still pretty. <break time="0.8s" /> She whispered. <break time="0.8s" /> The door opened. <break time="0.8s" /> And Jim stepped in and closed it. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked. <break time="0.8s" /> Thin and very serious. <break time="0.8s" /> Poor fellow. <break time="0.8s" /> He was only twenty two. <break time="0.8s" /> And he needed. <break time="0.8s" /> A new overcoat and gloves. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim stopped inside the door. <break time="0.8s" /> As still as a hunting dog. <break time="0.8s" /> That smells a bird. <break time="0.8s" /> His eyes were fixed upon Della. <break time="0.8s" /> And there was an expression in them. <break time="0.8s" /> That she could not read. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim, darling. <break time="0.8s" /> She cried. <break time="0.8s" /> Do not look at me that way. <break time="0.8s" /> I had my hair cut off and sold. <break time="0.8s" /> Because I could not live through Christmas. <break time="0.8s" /> Without giving you a present. <break time="0.8s" /> It will grow out again. <break time="0.8s" /> And my hair grows awfully fast.
